title: Tenant surge harmonizer and reservation drift action plan
creator: Priya Shah
description: Summary: Following the 2025-02-10 capacity incident where a multi-tenant surge triggered cascading evictions and elevated tail latency across two dedicated GPU clusters, this ticket consolidates the postmortem action items and proposes a coordinated implementation plan. Root causes identified in the postmortem: (1) reservation drift where long-running synthetic workloads and a bug in reservation reconciliation allowed tenants to consume more fractional capacity than allocated, (2) burst-credit decay set too permissively causing burst storms to persist longer than intended, and (3) lack of a fast noisy-neighbor detection signal in the allocator, delaying isolation for ~6m during the incident. This ticket designs a Tenant Surge Harmonizer (TSH) to limit and smooth transient spikes, a correction pass for reservation accounting, and burst-credit policy recalibration. The goal is to reduce correlated evictions, make QoS predictable, and provide operators both automatic and manual remediation knobs.
acceptance_criteria: TSH prototype deployed to canary pool with 99th percentile tail-latency improvement >= 25% on synthetic noisy workload
Reservation reconciliation job detects and corrects drift within 60s for >95% of misallocations in test harness
Burst-credit decay parameters adjusted and validated so that sustained burst consumption declines to baseline within 2 minutes under repeated spikes
Playbook and dashboard added to Console: operator can run 'ts-harmonic-reset' and observe affected tenants, with links to evictions and KV-cache metrics
E2E test in runtime CI that simulates 10 tenants with mixed short/long sequences and asserts no more than 1 eviction per 1000 requests after mitigations
action_items: Marcus Liu — Implement proportional burst governor (initial design: credits per tenant scaled by reservation and recent sustained throughput). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4312 — ETA 2w
Priya Shah — Reservation reconciliation corrective pass: idempotent scanner + fast reclaim path for fractional drift; include safe rollback hooks — ETA 1w
Ana Gomez — Add noisy-neighbor detector signal to allocator (stateless detector using rolling token consumption + kv-cache churn). Integrate with TSH for rapid fencing — ETA 10d
SRE (Lead: Jason Park) — Create console dashboard and alert rule: 'dedicated:tenant-noise-score > 0.7' with playbook link and automated read-only marker for canary runs — ETA 5d
Bench (Lead: Samir Patel) — Build synthetic tenant workload that reproduces reservation drift and burst storms; publish baseline graphs for tail latency, eviction rate, and reservation delta — ETA 6d
QA (Lead: Mei Chen) — E2E tests for eviction safety and graceful degrade paths; add CI gate for PRs touching allocator and reservation jobs — ETA 9d
Documentation — Runbook and post-incident writeup with commands, safe rollback steps, and telemetry interpretation examples — Owner: Priya Shah — ETA 4d

2025-02-22 Ana Gomez: Prototype noisy-neighbor detector added to allocator branch. Detector is intentionally conservative (low false positive) — flagged a couple synthetic tenants in bench runs. Need to decide fencing vs throttling behavior.

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive automatic tenant ejection reduces cluster-wide tail latency but risks customer-visible errors; we prefer a phased approach: (1) conservative detector + throttling for prod, (2) auto-fence only in canary/maintenance windows, (3) provide self-service tenant soft-reserve reset via Console for customers with transient surges. Long-term: integrate with billing alerts to correlate spikes with product events.
postmortem_summary: During the incident, reservation reconciliation lagged due to a stalled background job and a corner-case in fractional accounting. Combined with slow burst-credit decay, tenants could sustain above-reservation usage for multiple minutes, creating eviction cascades. Immediate mitigations we applied during the incident: manual soft-fence of top noisy tenants, emergency reservation decay tweak, and KV-cache warmup on reclaimed slots. This ticket operationalizes those mitigations into automated and tested systems.
release_plan: Week 1: Land reservation reconciliation race fix and deploy non-blocking detector to canary
Week 2: Deploy proportional burst governor to canary and run bench workloads; collect 2M request baseline
Week 3: Add Console dashboard, finalize playbook, and conduct runbook drill with SRE
Week 4: Progressive rollout to 10% of dedicated clusters with manual SRE gating, monitor for regressions, then 100% after one maintenance window
